source.display_title: 06/20/2026 - Johnathan and Ben - Primal Instinct — Lost

call.sequence_note: Second call with this prospect. The first, on 15 June, was cut short by a connection failure roughly fourteen minutes into discovery and rescheduled live to this slot. The rep opens by reading back his notes from it: 'I was going over just a few of the notes from our brief conversation earlier this week.'

rep.name: Ben Byrne
rep.location: Canada — back in his office, 9am local

setter.evidence: No setter involved. The prospect booked himself directly off an Instagram advert: 'I was scrolling on Instagram and the pop-up showed me this program with kettlebells' and 'this is why I scheduled a meeting on the website.'

prospect.name: Jonathan
prospect.occupation: IT technician working with B2B clients on site and from home. Previously ran his own photography business from 2022 until early 2026, when he returned to IT for a stable income before his son was born.
prospect.family_status: Married to Marie for two years; son born in the first month of 2026, roughly four months old. Currently saving to buy a house.
prospect.training_background: Started training seriously in the run-up to his wedding two years ago — gym, increased protein, supplements — and was committed to it. Stopped during a three-week honeymoon in Japan where he walked 20,000 steps a day and held his weight, then continued eating the same way in France without training and regained. Nothing at all for the past year. Researching calisthenics; had never heard of Trevor until about a week before the first call. Wants to train three times a week for 30-45 minutes and explicitly does not want to do more.

signals: Lost ground across a specific hard season — wedding, honeymoon, a failing photography business, a new baby and a career change back to IT

Carries visible regret that extends past fitness into business: 'all the goals I had set weren't really reached ... that's why my business hadn't grown up as I would have liked it to do, it's because I'm thinking too much'
Frames the whole thing as reclaiming agency: 'I don't want to endure my life anymore, I want to own it and to take the control of it'
Diverges from the classic rebuilder in that the target state is aspirational rather than restorative — his stated highest goal is a six-pack he has never had
Considered and rejected the_medically_constrained (nothing clinical disclosed) and skeptical_bargain_hunter (his cheap alternative, self-directed internet research, demonstrably did not work for him)

goals.text: Drop from 90 kg toward 75 kg and regain some muscle
A six-pack, named as his highest and least likely goal
Move and carry things freely without getting out of breath
Feel comfortable in his own body and mind
Prove to himself he can set a goal and actually reach it
Be a better provider and presence for his wife and new son — 'to give the best you can to your family'
Train three times a week for 30-45 minutes and no more, so it fits around his son
Take control of his life rather than let it happen to him

pains.text: Overthinks and over-plans instead of acting — 'I'm spending too much time in finding out how to reach that perfectly'
Doubts his own capacity to make the change — 'I'm always doubting, doubting of me ... I'm doubting that I can make that much of a change'
Sets goals and does not reach them, in fitness and in his failed photography business
No knowledge of nutrition or training and no time to acquire it — 'it's not my domain, so it [takes] me too much time'
Not prioritising his health and losing time to his phone — 'I'm not prioritizing right currently'
Dislikes cooking and currently leaves all food decisions to his wife
Afraid of injuring himself training unsupervised — 'you can harm yourself so fast doing things badly'
Money is tight after a wedding, a honeymoon, a new baby and saving for a house, and he only recently returned to salaried work
Gave up his photography business, which he loved, because it could not support the family

objections.raw_quote: The thing is, yeah, I don't have that much money on my account as I got married two years ago. So I don't know. I don't know. I will have to think about that.
objections.rep_response: Deflected briefly to how American clients pay ('A lot of our clients just throw it on a credit card'), then isolated properly: 'is there anything outside of just not having 6K available that's coming up for you? Or is it just the money?' Followed with a worth-it reframe tied to the prospect's own words about not sweating and feeling confident.

objections.raw_quote: I was, to be honest, I was looking to invest maybe a month, maybe a monthly, I was looking for 150, 150 or 200 a month, but right now, I don't even have that much money on my bank account
objections.rep_response: Noticed the hesitation honestly — 'You didn't sound very certain about that' — then probed the confusing $4,000 statement, asked whether his wife works, asked what he had set aside, and asked pointedly what his plan had been coming into the call knowing money would be discussed. Then presented the 3-month $4,000 tier and the $199/month Primal University.

objections.raw_quote: But I have to speak with my wife first because I can't decide that like this
objections.rep_response: Did not address it. He moved straight on to whether $100 could reach any tier and then introduced the light version of the programme. None of the spouse play ran, despite the rep having already established earlier in the call that Marie knows about the call and is supportive.

objections.raw_quote: And what about the three-month program? How does it cost? ... And for the non-personalized one, how old did it be?
objections.rep_response: Quoted $4,000 for three months and $199/month or $1,999/year for Primal University, and was straight about what the cheaper option lacks: 'It's not personalized, that's the thing ... if you're looking for personalization, you're gonna get that from working directly with Trevor.'

evidence: The rep disqualified him on budget: 'if you're looking at a budget of like $100, the coaching with Trevor, probably just out of the range right now'
Prospect declined every tier presented, including the $199/month option: 'I guess this wouldn't match because yeah I would like to have the coaching so maybe later'
Prospect: 'I'm not making some promises, I guess it will be not yet'
Rep closed by conceding it: 'you don't have the money, you don't have the money is what it is'

Counter-evidence toward follow_up: he said 'I will sleep on it and just let you know in a few days', asked for and confirmed the rep's email, and said he would try to put money aside — 'we'll see later how it goes'
Counter-evidence toward follow_up: the rep framed it softly as 'it's not a no, it's not now'
No next call booked, no deposit, no link, no date attached to any next step
outcome.next_step: Prospect to discuss with his wife and email the rep if anything changes. Nothing scheduled.

notable.note: An eighty-five minute call in which affordability was never tested until minute sixty-five, and the answer was that the prospect can reach roughly 100 to 200 euros a month against a $6,000 ask. He had disclosed the constraints in plain sight much earlier — a wedding and honeymoon two years ago, a photography business that failed, a four-month-old son, a career change taken specifically for income, and savings earmarked for a house. Discovery on the psychological side was genuinely good and the rep found the real blocker, which is that this prospect overthinks rather than acts. Two things to note for the rollup: the $4,000 three-month tier appears for the third time in this batch, and it is the sales process rather than the rep's technique that let a prospect with no discretionary income spend two calls and an hour and a half reaching a foregone conclusion.

quality.notes: Extensive inversion, worse than the batch average because the language barrier produces long overlapping turns. Whole rep questions are attributed to the prospect and vice versa — at 00:05:58, 00:18:42, 00:31:00 and throughout the pricing exchange from 01:19:51 the labels alternate mid-thought. A long stretch around 00:31:00 and again near 01:23:01 lost timestamps entirely and runs as unpunctuated text. The prospect is a non-native English speaker who repeatedly pauses to translate, which further fragments attribution. Roles resolved from content only.
